t.3.9.1: Having heard these words spoken by Vaidehī, who was devoted to her husband, Rāma, steadfast in dharma, then replied to Maithilī.
t.3.9.2: O queen, O daughter of Janaka, knower of dharma, you have spoken beneficial words out of affection, words befitting you and worthy of the family you invoke.
t.3.9.3: But what shall I say, O queen? You yourself have spoken these words: the bow is borne by kṣatriyas so that no cry of the distressed may be heard.
t.3.9.4: And those sages of rigorous vows in the Daṇḍaka forest, distressed, came to me themselves, O Sītā, and, though they are a refuge to others, sought refuge with me.
t.3.9.5: Living in the forest, devoted to dharma and subsisting on roots and fruits, they find no happiness, terrified by the rākṣasas of cruel deeds.
t.3.9.6: Time and again, those devoted to various religious observances in the forest are devoured by fearsome rākṣasas who live on human flesh.
t.3.9.7: Those sages dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest, the best of the twice-born, being devoured by the demons, said to me, "Protect us!"
t.3.9.8: But I, having heard the words thus fallen from their mouths, and having shown them reverent service at their feet, spoke these words.
t.3.9.9: Be gracious to me, for this is an unequalled shame for me, that I have been approached by such brahmins, who are themselves worthy to be approached, and that I had to say "What shall I do?" in the presence of the twice-born.
t.3.9.10: Having all come together, they spoke these words: “In the Daṇḍaka forest we are sorely tormented by many rākṣasas who take whatever form they wish, O Rāma; you ought to protect us.”
t.3.9.12: For us ascetics, devoted to austerity, who are oppressed by the rākṣasas and are searching for a refuge, you, sir, are the supreme refuge.
t.3.9.11: When the time for the fire-offering has come, and at the times of the parvan rites, O sinless one, the invincible flesh-eating rākṣasas would assail us.
t.3.9.13: Indeed, by the power of our austerities we are able to slay the night-roaming demons, but we do not wish to break the austerity we have gathered over so long a time.
t.3.9.14: Constant austerity is beset with many obstacles and is hard to practise, O Rāghava; therefore, even while being devoured by the rākṣasas, we do not release a curse.
t.3.9.15: Therefore protect us, who are being tormented by the Rākṣasas dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest, you together with your brother, for in this forest we have you as our protector.
t.3.9.16: And having heard these words, O daughter of Janaka, I promised the complete protection of the ṛṣis in the Daṇḍaka forest.
t.3.9.17: Having once given my promise to the sages, I shall not be able, while I live, to make it otherwise, for truth is ever dear to me.
t.3.9.18: I might give up my life, Sītā, or even you along with Lakṣmaṇa, but never a promise once made, especially one pledged to the brāhmaṇas.
t.3.9.19: Therefore, O Vaidehī, the protection of the ṛṣis must surely be carried out by me even had I not been asked; how much more so now that I have given my promise?
t.3.9.21: Having spoken these words to his beloved Sītā, the daughter of the king of Mithilā, the great-souled Rāma, bearing his bow, went together with Lakṣmaṇa to the delightful groves of the ascetics.
t.3.9.20: These words have been spoken by you out of affection and goodwill for me. I am well pleased, Sītā, for no one who is not dear is given counsel; and what you have said, O lovely one, is fitting and worthy of your family.
